text: Harbour City built an early 2-0 lead through patient, short passing with 17-pass build-ups culminating in Elias Okafor's goal (xG 0.111) and a long-range Marek Barros strike (xG 0.009) from a corner set-piece sequence [#905] [#975]. Despite Barros’ key role with 5 key passes, 2 assists, and 9 interceptions, Harbour City’s discipline was compromised after Joon Whitfield’s red card at 43’, reducing their defensive solidity [#870] [#975]. Seabrook Town embraced a 3-4-3 formation emphasizing wide, crossing play, and triggered a tactical shift at 65’ increasing press intensity (press from 0.66 to 0.84), directness (0.42 to 0.57), and line height (0.6 to 0.72) to regain control and exploit overloads on the flanks [#1361]. This press-and-attack mechanism enhanced their field tilt to 63.3% and boosted box touches (57 total) despite higher turnovers, facilitating 4 second-half goals by exploiting rapid transitions and counterattacks led by Kian Romano’s stoppage-time brace (xG 0.609 and 0.959) [#1448] [#1882] [#1906]. Harbour City’s PPDA (7.6) was outmatched by Seabrook’s more aggressive 5.5, evidencing the pressing trigger that enabled Seabrook’s comeback.

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals with an xG of 3.48, indicating strong finishing and chances created compared to Harbour City's 2 goals and xG of 1.0 [#905, #975, #1104, #1448, #1882, #1906].
- Marek Barros of Harbour City was key with 1 goal, 2 assists, 5 key passes, 9 interceptions and a 9.8 rating, despite his team losing [#975].
- Seabrook Town increased their press and directness after 65', leading to 4 second-half goals overcoming a 2-1 deficit [#1361, #1448].
- Harbour City led 2-0 by 47', but conceded 4 goals after the 53rd minute, with two late goals by Kian Romano at 90+2' and 90+3' to complete the comeback [#975, #1104, #1882, #1906].
- Joon Whitfield of Harbour City received a red card at 43', which likely impacted their defensive solidity [#870, #871].

- Seabrook Town’s late goals, especially Kian Romano’s brace in stoppage time, demonstrate effective counter-attacking play, as evidenced by quick regains and short, decisive passing leading to scoring chances within seconds of possession wins [1881,1882,1905,1906]. Their 3-4-3 formation likely facilitated this by providing width and quick outlets upfront to exploit spaces behind Harbour City’s advanced defensive line.

- Harbour City’s initial goals came from patient build-up involving many passes (17 passes over nearly a minute) reflecting their 4-2-3-1 style of patient short passing and possession. Marek Barros’ involvement as a creator and scorer aligns with his high key passes and assists stats, showing the team’s reliance on organized buildup and patience to create openings [904,905,975].

- Seabrook Town’s tactical shift around the 65th minute to higher pressing, more directness, and higher line height shows their attempt to regain control while chasing the game. This resulted in greater field tilt and box touches but also high turnovers, indicating a press-and-attack pattern likely designed to quickly recover possession and create attacking overloads [1361].

- Barros’ long-range successful goal (44m) from a corner sequence highlights Harbour City’s use of set pieces as an additional attacking tactic, reflecting their disciplined positioning and ability to exploit moments even when not dominant in open play [975]. 

- Despite Harbour City’s patient style and reasonable pass accuracy, Seabrook Town’s wider formation and crossing play style generated more shots and big chances, especially later in the match, showing Seabrook's effectiveness exploiting width and creating overloads on the flanks for crosses and penetrating passes [team_styles, shots and big_chances stats].
